readings.title: Elihu Speaks
readings.subtitle: Anger at Job and His Friends
readings.text: [Job 32:1] So these three men ceased answering Iyoḇ, because he was righteous in his own eyes. [2] Then the wrath of Elihu, son of Baraḵel the Buzite, of the clan of Ram, burned against Iyoḇ. His wrath burned because he declared himself right rather than <dn>Elohim</dn>. [3] And his wrath burned against his three friends, because they had found no answer, and they had declared Iyoḇ wrong. [4] Now Elihu had waited to speak to Iyoḇ, because they were older than he. [5] And when Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of these three men, his wrath burned. [6] And Elihu, son of Baraḵel the Buzite, answered and said: “I am young in years, and you are very old; therefore I was afraid, and feared to declare my knowledge to you. [7] “I said, ‘Days should speak, and many years should teach wisdom.’ [8] “But there is a spirit in man, and the breath of the <dn>Almighty</dn> gives them understanding. [9] “Great men are not always wise, nor do the aged always understand right-ruling. [10] “Therefore I have said, ‘Listen to me, let me also declare my knowledge.’ [11] “See, I waited for your words, I listened to your reasonings, while you searched out what to say. [12] “And I paid close attention to you, and see, not one of you reproved Iyoḇ, nor answered his words. [13] “Lest you say, ‘We have found wisdom’; <dn>El</dn> drives him away, not man. [14] “Now he has not ordered words against me, so I shall not answer him with your words. [15] “They have been broken down, they have not answered again, words have moved away from them. [16] “And I waited, because they did not speak, because they stood still, they answered no more. [17] “Let me answer, I also, my portion. Let me declare my knowledge, I also. [18] “For I am filled with words; the spirit within me distresses me. [19] “See, within me it is like wine not opened, it bursts like new wineskins. [20] “Let me speak, so that I find relief; let me open my lips and answer. [21] “Let me not show partiality to anyone, nor let me flatter any man. [22] “For I do not know to flatter, else my <dn>Maker</dn> would soon take me away.

readings.title: Elihu Challenges Job
readings.subtitle: God Speaks in Various Ways
readings.text: [Job 33:1] “But please, hear my speech, O Iyoḇ, and listen to all my words. [2] “See, please, I have opened my mouth; my tongue has spoken in my mouth. [3] “My words come from the uprightness of my heart, and my lips speak knowledge clearly. [4] “The Spirit of <dn>El</dn> has made me, and the breath of the <dn>Almighty</dn> gives me life. [5] “If you are able, answer me, array yourself before me, stand up. [6] “See, I am as your mouth before <dn>El</dn>; I also have been formed out of clay. [7] “See, no fear of me should terrify you, nor my hand be heavy on you. [8] “You have surely spoken in my hearing, and I have heard the sound of your words, saying, [9] ‘I am pure, without transgression; I am innocent, and there is no crookedness in me. [10] ‘See, <dn>He</dn> finds occasions against me, <dn>He</dn> counts me as <dn>His</dn> enemy; [11] ‘<dn>He</dn> puts my feet in the stocks, <dn>He</dn> watches all my paths.’ [12] “See, in this you are not right – I answer you, for <dn>Eloah</dn> is greater than man. [13] “Why do you strive against <dn>Him</dn>? For <dn>He</dn> does not give account of any of <dn>His</dn> matters. [14] “For <dn>El</dn> speaks once, or twice – though one does not notice it – [15] “In a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falls upon men, while slumbering on the bed, [16] “Then <dn>He</dn> opens the ears of men, and seals their instruction. [17] “To turn man from his deed, and conceal pride from man, [18] “<dn>He</dn> keeps back his being from the pit, and his life from passing away by the sword. [19] “Also man is chastened with pain on his bed, and with strong pain in many of his bones, [20] “So that his life loathes bread, and his being desirable food. [21] “His flesh wastes away from sight, and his bones stick out which were not seen. [22] “And his being draws near to the pit, and his life to the destroyers. [23] “If there is a messenger for him, a mediator, one among a thousand, to show man <dn>His</dn> straightness, [24] “Then <dn>He</dn> shows favour to him, and says, ‘Deliver him from going down to the Pit; I have found a ransom’; [25] “His flesh becomes fresher than a child’s; he returns to the days of his youth. [26] “He prays to <dn>Eloah</dn>, and <dn>He</dn> accepts him, and he sees <dn>His</dn> face with joy, and <dn>He</dn> restores to man his righteousness. [27] “He sings before men and says, ‘I have sinned, and perverted what was right, and it did not profit me.’ [28] “<dn>He</dn> has redeemed my being from going down to the Pit, and my life sees the light. [29] “See, <dn>El</dn> does all these, twice, three times with a man, [30] “To bring back his being from the Pit, to be enlightened with the light of the living. [31] “Pay attention, O Iyoḇ, listen to me; keep silent, and let me speak. [32] “If there are words, answer me; speak, for I desire to declare you right. [33] “If not, listen to me; keep silent, and let me teach you wisdom.”

readings.title: Elihu Vindicates God
readings.subtitle: God Cannot Be Unjust
readings.text: [Job 34:1] And Elihu answered and said: [2] “Hear my words, you wise men; and give ear to me, you who have knowledge. [3] “For the ear tries words as the palate tastes food. [4] “Let us choose justice for ourselves; let us know among ourselves what is good. [5] “For Iyoḇ has said, ‘I am righteous, but <dn>El</dn> has turned aside my right-ruling. [6] ‘Should I lie concerning my right-ruling? My wound is incurable, though I am without transgression.’ [7] “What man is like Iyoḇ, who drinks scorn like water, [8] “And travels in company with the workers of wickedness, and walks with men of wickedness? [9] “For he has said, ‘It profits a man nothing that he should delight in <dn>Elohim</dn>.’ [10] “Therefore listen to me, you men of heart: Far be it from <dn>El</dn> to do wickedness, and from the <dn>Almighty</dn> to do unrighteousness. [11] “For <dn>He</dn> repays man according to his work, and makes man to find a reward according to his way. [12] “And truly, <dn>El</dn> does not do wickedly, nor does the <dn>Almighty</dn> pervert right-ruling. [13] “Who appointed <dn>Him</dn> over the earth? Or who set the whole world in order? [14] “If <dn>He</dn> should set <dn>His</dn> heart on it, if <dn>He</dn> should gather to <dn>Himself</dn> <dn>His</dn> Spirit and <dn>His</dn> breath, [15] “All flesh would expire together, and man return to dust. [16] “If you have understanding, hear this; give ear to the voice of my words. [17] “Should one who hates right-ruling govern? Or would you declare wrong a mighty one who is righteous? [18] “Is it fitting to say to a sovereign, ‘Belial,’ or to nobles, ‘Wicked’? [19] “Yet <dn>He</dn> does not show partiality to princes, nor regards the rich more than the poor; for they are all the work of <dn>His</dn> hands. [20] “In a moment they die, in the middle of the night; the people are shaken and pass away, and the mighty are taken away without a hand. [21] “For <dn>His</dn> eyes are on the ways of man, and <dn>He</dn> sees all his steps. [22] “There is no darkness nor death-shadow where the workers of wickedness hide themselves. [23] “For <dn>He</dn> need not set a time for a man to go before <dn>El</dn> in judgment. [24] “<dn>He</dn> breaks in pieces mighty ones without inquiry, and sets others in their place. [25] “Therefore <dn>He</dn> knows their works, and <dn>He</dn> overthrows them in the night, and they are crushed. [26] “<dn>He</dn> strikes them as wicked, in the open sight of others, [27] “Because they turned back from <dn>Him</dn>, and did not consider any of <dn>His</dn> ways, [28] “So that they caused the cry of the poor to come to <dn>Him</dn>; for <dn>He</dn> hears the cry of the afflicted. [29] “When <dn>He</dn> is quiet, who then might condemn? And when <dn>He</dn> hides <dn>His</dn> face, who then sees <dn>Him</dn>, whether it is against a nation or a man alone? – [30] “That the defiled one should not reign, lest the people be ensnared. [31] “For has anyone said to <dn>El</dn>, ‘I have borne chastisement, I do not offend, [32] ‘Teach me what I do not see; if I have done unrighteousness, I do it no more’? [33] “Should <dn>He</dn> repay it according to your mind, because you refused it? You must choose, and not I; therefore speak what you know. [34] “Men of heart say to me, and a wise man who listens to me: [35] ‘Iyoḇ speaks without knowledge, and his words are without wisdom.’ [36] “Would that Iyoḇ were tried to the limit, because his answers are like those of men of wickedness! [37] “For he adds rebellion to his sin; he claps his hands among us, and multiplies his words against <dn>El</dn>.”
